sentences: ARRIVAL describes a deterministic walk in a directed graph whose vertices alternate between two outgoing choices on successive visits.
The decision task asks which designated destination the walk eventually reaches.
The source notes efficiently verifiable certificates for either answer, placing the problem in NP intersect coNP.
It improves exponential algorithms to a subexponential bound and gives a polynomial-time algorithm for almost acyclic graphs.
The remaining project is to decide whether all instances can be solved in polynomial time without explicitly following a walk that may be exponentially long.
